subject: POC success metrics & observation protocol — next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena@nubiq.com>, Amit Shah <amit.shah@nubiqa.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC success metrics & observation protocol — next steps

Hi Lena / Amit —

Great to connect earlier today. Per our call, here’s a concise post-call recap with the proposed evaluation approach and ownership so we can get the POC started next week. I attached a short observation protocol and a sample dataset so you can see the inputs we’ll use.

Goal of the POC (2 weeks): validate that Redwood inference can serve Nubiq’s summary pipeline within the latency and cost targets while matching the quality bar you set today.

Success criteria (binary + graded):
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency < 650ms for 1k-token job (binary pass/fail).
- Cost: cost-per-1000-requests within 20% of your current baseline (graded: pass / marginal / fail).
- Quality: automatic overlap metrics + human-graded rubric: average human grade >= 4.0/5 across sampled prompts (see rubric below).
- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% (HTTP 5xx / timeouts).

Evaluation plan (two parallel tracks):
1) Offline grading (recommended first 5 business days):
  - We run a 200-sample offline eval against your historical dataset that you provided. Metrics: ROUGE-L, BERTScore, and our human rubric.
  - Owner: Redwood SE (Marissa) will produce the grade table and flag any systematic failure modes.

2) Online shadow (can start Day 3):
  - We shadow live traffic in read-only mode for 3 days to capture distributional differences and observe latency under realistic load. No user-facing traffic will be served by Redwood during shadow.
  - Owner: Nubiq infra + Redwood ops (Karthik) to approve routing and sampling.
  - Data flows: only input text and request metadata will be sent; we will NOT persist PII.

Human grading rubric (sample):
- 5 = Expert-level: factual, concise, matches intent, no verbosity
- 4 = Strong: minor omissions but acceptable
- 3 = Needs improvement: misses critical detail or hallucination risk
- 2 = Poor: likely unusable without edits
- 1 = Wrong or hallucinated

Timeline (proposed):
- Day 0 (tomorrow): MSA & data access checklist signed; provide test dataset (you already shared sample).
- Day 1–3: Offline eval results + quick tuning (hyperparams/prompt adjustments)
- Day 3–6: Start online shadowing (3 full business days)
- Day 7 (end of week): Consolidated POC report + recommendation (go/no-go)

Immediate asks from Nubiq:
- Confirm the 2-week window is OK and that you can provide the 2k anonymized historical records we discussed.
- Approve the online shadow sampling percentage (I propose 5% of traffic for initial run).

Attachments: redwood-observation-protocol.pdf, nubiq-sample-dataset.csv, poc-access-checklist.docx

Next steps: if you confirm, I’ll schedule a kickoff for Wednesday 10am PT and loop in our ops lead for sandbox provisioning.

Thanks —
Karthik

Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

From: Lena Park <lena@nubiq.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Amit Shah <amit.shah@nubiqa.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC success metrics & observation protocol — next steps

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful and exactly the clarity we needed. A few quick points from our side:

1) Timeline: we’re happy to aim for the 2-week window but can we compress the offline eval to Day 0–2 and start shadowing on Day 2? We have an internal stakeholder asking for faster visibility.
2) Dataset: we will provide 2,200 anonymized records by EOD Tuesday. Will those be enough for the offline grade?
3) Security/Compliance: our security team requests a brief note confirming that no PII will be persisted and that access logs are available for the POC period. Can your ops team confirm?
4) Procurement: procurement wants a draft SOW + estimate before we flip the test traffic switch. Any chance you can provide a short SOW template and an estimated cost band now?

Assignees from Nubiq: Amit (infra lead) will coordinate sandbox/networking. I will be the product lead for grading and acceptance.

If you can send updated timeline and the SOW template, we’ll prioritize. Kickoff Wednesday 10am PT works for us.

—Lena
Lena Park
Head of Product | Nubiq Analytics
[lena@nubiq.com]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lena Park <lena@nubiq.com>, Amit Shah <amit.shah@nubiqa.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC success metrics & observation protocol — next steps

Karthik / Sean —

Looping in a short SE ops note so we’re aligned on what the offline grading and shadow will require from a config and ownership perspective. I’m fine with compressing the offline eval to Day 0–2 (we’ll prioritize automated runs). Quick checklist: 

- Offline eval: I will run the 200–400 sample pass (depends on the final dataset) and produce the grade sheet (ROUGE-L, BERTScore, human scores). Deliverable: grade_table.csv in shared Drive. Owner: Marissa (SE).
- Shadow config: need sampling hook from Nubiq (Amit) — we’ll take 5% to start; if distribution variance is high we can increase. Owner: Nubiq infra + Redwood ops (Karthik) for routing.
- Model variant & tuning: start with open-model-v2-8q; if quality < 4.0 we’ll try prompt tuning and a 4-bit quantized variant. Owner: Marissa.
- Security ask: Redwood ops confirms NO PII persistence during POC; logs retained for 30 days and available on request. (Karthik — can ops send confirmation / short note to Lena?)
- SOW: I’ve attached a one-page SOW template that outlines scope, timeline, and an estimated cost band for shadowing. I marked placeholders for numbers we should fill after API / request volume estimates.

I’ll upload the grade sheet and a short summary doc to the Drive folder listed in the kickoff invite.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
